requirements.quote:
The domain begins at IN-ADDR.ARPA and has a substructure which follows
the Internet addressing structure.
requirements.condition: When representing Internet address-to-name or gateway-location data in this special domain.
requirements.required_behavior: Root the special address domain at IN-ADDR.ARPA.
requirements.why_checkable: The domain suffix used by address-domain construction is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
Domain names in the IN-ADDR.ARPA domain are defined to have up to four
labels in addition to the IN-ADDR.ARPA suffix.
requirements.condition: For a domain name in the IN-ADDR.ARPA address hierarchy.
requirements.required_behavior: Use at most four labels before the IN-ADDR.ARPA suffix.
requirements.why_checkable: The count of labels preceding the fixed suffix can be checked.

requirements.quote:
Each label represents
one octet of an Internet address,
requirements.condition: For each address label before the IN-ADDR.ARPA suffix.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent exactly one Internet-address octet per label.
requirements.why_checkable: The mapping between address octets and generated name labels can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Each label represents
one octet of an Internet address, and is expressed as a character string
for a decimal value in the range 0-255 (with leading zeros omitted
except in the case of a zero octet which is represented by a single
zero).
requirements.condition: For each address label before the IN-ADDR.ARPA suffix.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the octet as a decimal character string.
requirements.why_checkable: The name encoder can be checked for decimal textual output.

requirements.quote:
Each label represents
one octet of an Internet address, and is expressed as a character string
for a decimal value in the range 0-255 (with leading zeros omitted
except in the case of a zero octet which is represented by a single
zero).
requirements.condition: For each address label before the IN-ADDR.ARPA suffix.
requirements.required_behavior: Constrain its represented numeric value to the inclusive range 0 through 255.
requirements.why_checkable: The representable octet range and boundary cases can be checked.

requirements.quote:
Each label represents
one octet of an Internet address, and is expressed as a character string
for a decimal value in the range 0-255 (with leading zeros omitted
except in the case of a zero octet which is represented by a single
zero).
requirements.condition: When encoding a nonzero octet in an IN-ADDR.ARPA address label.
requirements.required_behavior: Omit leading zeros from the decimal label.
requirements.why_checkable: Nonzero octets can be encoded and their leading characters checked.

requirements.quote:
Each label represents
one octet of an Internet address, and is expressed as a character string
for a decimal value in the range 0-255 (with leading zeros omitted
except in the case of a zero octet which is represented by a single
zero).
requirements.condition: When encoding a zero octet in an IN-ADDR.ARPA address label.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the octet by the single character 0.
requirements.why_checkable: Zero-octet encoding has an exact expected label.

requirements.quote:
Host addresses are represented by domain names that have all four labels
specified.
requirements.condition: When representing a complete Internet host address under IN-ADDR.ARPA.
requirements.required_behavior: Specify all four address labels.
requirements.why_checkable: The generated host-address name must contain four octet labels.

requirements.quote:
Host addresses are represented by domain names that have all four labels
specified.  Thus data for Internet address 10.2.0.52 is located at
domain name 52.0.2.10.IN-ADDR.ARPA.  The reversal, though awkward to
read, allows zones to be delegated which are exactly one network of
address space.
requirements.condition: When constructing the IN-ADDR.ARPA domain name for an Internet host address.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the address octets in reverse order before the IN-ADDR.ARPA suffix.
requirements.why_checkable: A host address and its reverse-domain name provide a deterministic mapping to check.

requirements.quote:
Address nodes are used to hold pointers to primary host names
in the normal domain space.
requirements.condition: For a full host-address node in the IN-ADDR.ARPA domain.
requirements.required_behavior: Hold pointers to the primary name of that host in the normal domain space.
requirements.why_checkable: The association between a full address node and the corresponding primary host name is inspectable.

requirements.quote:
Network numbers correspond to some non-terminal nodes at various depths
in the IN-ADDR.ARPA domain, since Internet network numbers are either 1,
2, or 3 octets.
requirements.condition: When representing an Internet network number in the IN-ADDR.ARPA domain.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a non-terminal node whose one, two, or three address labels correspond to the one, two, or three octets of the network number.
requirements.why_checkable: Network-number length can be compared with the depth of its node.

requirements.quote:
Network nodes are used to hold pointers to the primary
host names of gateways attached to that network.
requirements.condition: For a network node in the IN-ADDR.ARPA domain.
requirements.required_behavior: Hold pointers to primary host names of gateways attached to that network.
requirements.why_checkable: The network-node pointer targets can be checked against gateway identities and network attachments.

requirements.quote:
Gateways will also have host level
pointers at their fully qualified addresses.
requirements.condition: For gateways represented in the IN-ADDR.ARPA domain.
requirements.required_behavior: Also provide host-level pointers at their fully qualified addresses.
requirements.why_checkable: Gateway address nodes can be checked for the required host-level pointers.

requirements.quote:
Both the gateway pointers at network nodes and the normal host pointers
at full address nodes use the PTR RR to point back to the primary domain
names of the corresponding hosts.
requirements.condition: For gateway pointers at network nodes and host pointers at full address nodes in IN-ADDR.ARPA.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the pointers using PTR resource records.
requirements.why_checkable: The RR type used to represent both kinds of pointer is directly checkable.

requirements.quote:
Thus a program which wanted to locate gateways on net 10 would originate
a query of the form QTYPE=PTR, QCLASS=IN, QNAME=10.IN-ADDR.ARPA.  It
would receive two RRs in response:
requirements.condition: When constructing an IN-ADDR.ARPA query to locate gateways on an Internet network, as in the network-10 query described here.
requirements.required_behavior: Set QTYPE to PTR.
requirements.why_checkable: The gateway-discovery query type can be inspected independently of the sample response data.

requirements.quote:
Thus a program which wanted to locate gateways on net 10 would originate
a query of the form QTYPE=PTR, QCLASS=IN, QNAME=10.IN-ADDR.ARPA.  It
would receive two RRs in response:
requirements.condition: When constructing an IN-ADDR.ARPA query to locate gateways on an Internet network, as in the network-10 query described here.
requirements.required_behavior: Set QCLASS to IN.
requirements.why_checkable: The gateway-discovery query class can be inspected independently of the sample response data.

requirements.quote:
A resolver which wanted to find the host name corresponding to Internet
host address 10.0.0.6 would pursue a query of the form QTYPE=PTR,
QCLASS=IN, QNAME=6.0.0.10.IN-ADDR.ARPA, and would receive:
requirements.condition: When constructing an IN-ADDR.ARPA query to obtain the name for an Internet host address, as in the address-10.0.0.6 query described here.
requirements.required_behavior: Set QTYPE to PTR.
requirements.why_checkable: The reverse-hostname query type can be checked independently of the particular host in the example.

requirements.quote:
A resolver which wanted to find the host name corresponding to Internet
host address 10.0.0.6 would pursue a query of the form QTYPE=PTR,
QCLASS=IN, QNAME=6.0.0.10.IN-ADDR.ARPA, and would receive:
requirements.condition: When constructing an IN-ADDR.ARPA query to obtain the name for an Internet host address, as in the address-10.0.0.6 query described here.
requirements.required_behavior: Set QCLASS to IN.
requirements.why_checkable: The reverse-hostname query class can be checked independently of the particular host in the example.

requirements.quote:
The program could then originate QTYPE=A, QCLASS=IN queries for MILNET-
GW.ISI.EDU. and GW.LCS.MIT.EDU. to discover the Internet addresses of
these gateways.
requirements.condition: If a program chooses the optional follow-up lookup to discover Internet addresses of gateway names returned by the preceding lookup.
requirements.required_behavior: Use QTYPE=A for the optional address query.
requirements.why_checkable: The chosen follow-up query can be checked for the specified RR type; the lookup itself remains optional.

requirements.quote:
The program could then originate QTYPE=A, QCLASS=IN queries for MILNET-
GW.ISI.EDU. and GW.LCS.MIT.EDU. to discover the Internet addresses of
these gateways.
requirements.condition: If a program chooses the optional follow-up lookup to discover Internet addresses of gateway names returned by the preceding lookup.
requirements.required_behavior: Use QCLASS=IN for the optional address query.
requirements.why_checkable: The chosen follow-up query can be checked for the Internet class; the lookup itself remains optional.

requirements.quote:
- Gateways will often have two names in separate domains, only
     one of which can be primary.
requirements.condition: When a gateway has two names in separate domains.
requirements.required_behavior: Designate only one of the gateway names as primary.
requirements.why_checkable: Primary-name selection can be checked for uniqueness.

requirements.quote:
- Systems that use the domain database to initialize their
     routing tables must start with enough gateway information to
     guarantee that they can access the appropriate name server.
requirements.condition: For a system that uses the domain database to initialize its routing tables.
requirements.required_behavior: Start with enough gateway information to reach the appropriate name server.
requirements.why_checkable: A bootstrap scenario can check that a route to the needed name server exists before DNS-derived routing-table initialization.

requirements.quote:
- The gateway data only reflects the existence of a gateway in a
     manner equivalent to the current HOSTS.TXT file.  It doesn't
     replace the dynamic availability information from GGP or EGP.
requirements.condition: When using the IN-ADDR.ARPA gateway data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use gateway-existence data as a replacement for dynamic availability information from GGP or EGP.
requirements.why_checkable: The interpretation of gateway records can be checked to ensure existence records do not substitute for dynamic gateway availability.
